ui.sourceNote: Mission facts and images from NASA and the Chandra X-ray Center. Follow the official sources for operational updates.

newhorizons.name: New Horizons
newhorizons.intro: The first close encounter with Pluto opened a window onto the icy worlds beyond Neptune. New Horizons continued to Arrokoth, carrying its exploration into the Kuiper Belt.
newhorizons.heroAlt: NASA illustration of the New Horizons spacecraft
newhorizons.heroCaption: New Horizons · illustration · NASA / Johns Hopkins APL / SwRI

orbit.title: A one-way journey to the outer solar system
orbit.body: Jupiter's gravity accelerated the probe toward Pluto. Both Pluto and Arrokoth were flyby targets: New Horizons did not enter orbit around either world.

labels.description: Flight sequence from Earth via Jupiter and Pluto to Arrokoth

timeline.title: Leaving Earth
timeline.body: An Atlas V launches the spacecraft toward the outer planets.

timeline.title: Jupiter gravity assist
timeline.body: The encounter shortens the journey to Pluto by about three years.

timeline.title: Pluto and its moons
timeline.body: A brief encounter reveals an unexpectedly varied icy system.

timeline.title: Arrokoth flyby
timeline.body: The probe explores a second Kuiper Belt world up close.

newhorizons.instrumentIntro: Seven investigations combine imaging, spectroscopy, radio science and measurements of the space environment.

instruments.name: LORRI + Ralph
instruments.body: Detailed images, colour mapping and infrared spectra reveal terrain and surface composition.

instruments.name: Alice + REX
instruments.body: Ultraviolet spectroscopy and a radio experiment investigate atmospheres.

instruments.name: SWAP + PEPSSI
instruments.body: Particle instruments study the solar wind and energetic particles along the flight path.

instruments.name: Student Dust Counter
instruments.body: A student-built detector measures dust impacts far from the Sun.

newhorizons.galleryTitle: An icy world in unexpected detail
newhorizons.galleryIntro: Images from the 2015 encounter. Enhanced colours reveal surface differences and atmospheric structure.

gallery.title: Pluto in colour
gallery.alt: Enhanced-colour Pluto with a bright heart-shaped region
gallery.body: Ralph's visible and infrared images bring out subtle differences across Pluto's surface.

gallery.title: Charon's contrasting terrain
gallery.alt: Charon with a dark reddish polar region and fractured terrain
gallery.body: Enhanced colours highlight the reddish north pole of Pluto's largest moon.

gallery.title: A blue atmospheric haze
gallery.alt: The crescent of Pluto outlined by a thin blue haze
gallery.body: Looking back after the flyby, New Horizons reveals layers of haze above Pluto's limb.

juno.name: Juno
juno.intro: A solar-powered explorer of Jupiter's atmosphere, interior and magnetic environment. Juno links dramatic cloudscapes with measurements that help explain how a giant planet works.
juno.heroAlt: NASA illustration of Juno and its three solar-array wings

stats.label: Jupiter arrival
stats.note: Orbit insertion: 5 July UTC / 4 July PDT

stats.label: Orbit
stats.note: Close passes over the cloud tops

orbit.title: From pole to pole
orbit.body: An elongated orbit brings Juno close to Jupiter during each perijove, then carries it far away. Moon flybys have changed the orbit during the extended mission.

labels.description: Schematic elongated polar orbit of Juno around Jupiter

timeline.title: Launch
timeline.body: Juno begins a five-year journey to Jupiter.

timeline.title: Earth gravity assist
timeline.body: A return to Earth provides the boost needed to reach Jupiter.

timeline.title: Jupiter orbit insertion
timeline.body: A main-engine burn lets Jupiter capture the spacecraft.

timeline.title: A wider exploration
timeline.body: The extended mission includes close encounters with Ganymede, Europa and Io.

juno.instrumentIntro: Complementary instruments connect Jupiter's deep atmosphere to its powerful magnetic environment.

instruments.name: MWR
instruments.body: The microwave radiometer probes water and ammonia beneath the visible cloud tops.

instruments.name: JunoCam + JIRAM
instruments.body: Visible-light and infrared imaging reveal clouds, auroras and features on Jupiter's moons.

instruments.name: MAG + Gravity Science
instruments.body: Magnetic measurements and radio tracking investigate the field and the planet's internal mass distribution.

instruments.name: JADE · JEDI · Waves · UVS
instruments.body: Particles, plasma waves and ultraviolet emissions reveal the physics of Jupiter's auroras.

juno.galleryIntro: JunoCam data processed by citizen scientists. Credits and original processing details accompany each image.

gallery.title: Clouds in motion
gallery.alt: Jupiter's swirling cloud bands and a bright oval storm
gallery.body: An enhanced-colour view from February 2017 highlights a storm in the southern hemisphere.

gallery.title: The Great Red Spot
gallery.alt: Jupiter's Great Red Spot surrounded by turbulent cloud bands
gallery.body: This July 2017 view uses a natural-colour rendering of Jupiter's most recognisable storm.

gallery.title: Io's south polar region
gallery.alt: Jupiter's volcanic moon Io seen over its south polar region
gallery.body: The April 2024 encounter adds a new perspective on the volcanic moon.

chandra.name: Chandra
chandra.intro: Exploded stars, hot gas and matter around black holes shine in X-rays. Chandra observes this energetic Universe from above Earth's absorbing atmosphere.
chandra.heroAlt: NASA illustration of the Chandra X-ray Observatory in space

orbit.title: A high orbit for long observations
orbit.body: Chandra follows an elongated Earth orbit, reaching roughly 140,000 km in altitude. Long stretches far from Earth allow extended observations of faint X-ray sources.

labels.description: Schematic high elliptical orbit of Chandra around Earth

timeline.title: Launch on Columbia
timeline.body: The STS-93 crew deploys the observatory into space.

timeline.title: First light
timeline.body: Cassiopeia A reveals the fine structure of a supernova remnant.

timeline.title: The Bullet Cluster
timeline.body: X-ray and lensing maps provide strong evidence for dark matter.

timeline.title: A quarter century
timeline.body: Chandra marks 25 years since launch with a rich archive of discoveries.

chandra.instrumentIntro: Two focal-plane detectors and two sets of gratings turn incoming X-rays into images and spectra.

instruments.name: ACIS
instruments.body: CCD detectors record both the positions and energies of X-ray photons.

instruments.name: HRC
instruments.body: The high-resolution camera records fine spatial detail and precise photon arrival times.

instruments.name: HETG
instruments.body: High-energy transmission gratings spread X-rays into spectra for detailed analysis.

instruments.name: LETG
instruments.body: Low-energy transmission gratings reveal spectral features at longer X-ray wavelengths.

chandra.galleryIntro: X-ray energies are mapped to visible colours. Composite views can combine several telescopes and measurements.

gallery.title: Cassiopeia A
gallery.alt: Multicoloured X-ray shell of the supernova remnant Cassiopeia A
gallery.body: Different X-ray energies trace hot debris from an exploded star.

gallery.title: The Crab's central engine
gallery.alt: Bright rings and jets around the Crab Nebula pulsar in X-rays
gallery.body: A spinning neutron star powers rings and jets of energetic particles.

gallery.title: The Bullet Cluster
gallery.alt: Composite of colliding galaxy clusters with pink gas and blue mass maps
gallery.body: Pink marks hot gas; blue shows mass inferred from lensing. Their separation is evidence for dark matter.
